findings.location: Methods p.4 and Results p.4 vs data/rec_data_raw.csv
findings.evidence: The Methods say the forms were 'independently coded by two team members' and that 'all coding matched except for 1 instance regarding sample size calculation' (footnote 3). The released data file has one row per institution with a single set of codes (sample_size, justification, calculation) and no coder identifier, so the second coder's codes cannot be recovered and the reported agreement cannot be checked from the materials. The four cases in which coder 2 chose 'indirectly requested' where coder 1 chose 'requested' are also not marked in the data.

findings.location: Methods p.3-4; Figure 1 caption p.4-5; data/rec_data_raw.csv
findings.evidence: The paper reports that 7 RECs declined to share their form and that 6 of them cited an online submission system, and that the sample is therefore biased towards text-document forms. The data file records form_available as 'declined' (1 US) and 'declined_online' (US 3 + UK 3 = 6), which reproduces the 7 and the 6 (bp_out/tables/recount.json), but the paper does not report how many of the 20 included forms came from online portals or from private sharing (US 3 private + UK 2 private = 5 of 20 by our count), so the size of the bias cannot be judged.

The headline '6 of 20' is stable, but the quantity it summarises is definition-dependent: counting only explicit requests gives 3 of 20 (15%) instead of 6 of 20 (30%), and the US share is 40% with indirect requests counted and 20% without (universes 4 vs 10). The paper's own Results sentence uses the two definitions for the two countries (US 40% = explicit + indirect, UK 20% = explicit + indirect of 10, i.e. 2/10; explicit only would be 10%).

Claim 'fewer than half of the sampled REC/IRB template forms request a sample size calculation' holds in 23 of 24 universes (96%). Forks: scope (20 university forms vs also the 3 national forms), calculation definition (explicit + indirect = paper's 6/20 vs explicit only = 3/20), denominator (20 included forms vs 33 sampled institutions), country (pooled vs US vs UK). The single universe where it fails is the most inclusive one: national forms added and US only, 6/12 = 50.0% (NIH drug/device + NIH behavioural + 4 of 10 US university forms).
